messages:
jamie: quick heads-up — ran a reservation sensitivity for next quarter. baseline util at 65%, NA vs EU reserved SKU pricing diverges more than I expected. thinking we should rebalance some new commits toward eu-west for inference-heavy customers. any red flags?
vikas: what % shift are you thinking? we've got obligations in NA that are pretty sticky because of dedicated pools.
jamie: proposal: move 30% of the new committed GPUs for q3 to eu-west, focus on A100/80GB there. model: assume 65% util, 12h avg runtime per pod/day. raw delta looks like ~12% lower $/token in EU once you include reduced egress for eu-custs.
marta: can you paste the calc? I want to sanity check the egress assumptions (we were counting 50% of traffic as cross-region previously).
jamie: sure — here's the quick snippet I used:
```
# simplified per-GPU math (monthly)
NA_reserved_price = 12000   # $ per GPU/month (example)
EU_reserved_price = 10500   # $ per GPU/month
util = 0.65
monthly_tokens_per_gpu = util * 24 * 3600 * 50  # ~50 tokens/sec avg for our inference mix
unit_cost_na = NA_reserved_price / monthly_tokens_per_gpu
unit_cost_eu = EU_reserved_price / monthly_tokens_per_gpu
delta_pct = (unit_cost_na - unit_cost_eu) / unit_cost_na * 100
```
marta: okay that looks fine for the rough calc. two caveats: 1) mixed SKU availability — H100s are still more NA-centric in the cheapest reserved offers; 2) latency-sensitive customers in NA may not benefit.
lisa: also check committed term lengths. EU committed offers have discounts for 1y vs 3y that change the breakeven. if we can keep 12-months, the EU advantage shrinks a bit.
jamie: good call. I ran a scenario matrix — attached small table below (quick paste):
Region,SKU,Reserved$/GPU,EstimatedUtil,AdjUnit$/token
NA,A100,12000,0.65,0.000023
EU,A100,10500,0.65,0.000020
NA,H100,16000,0.62,0.000030
EU,H100,15000,0.62,0.000028

vikas: interesting. For the H100 line the savings are smaller but still non-trivial. What about spot mix? if we increase spot+reserved hybrid in NA, maybe we can keep capacity without shifting regions.
marta: agree — we should compare these two plays: (A) region-shift some reserved commits to EU vs (B) increase NA spot capacity + smaller reserved in NA.
jamie: quick PS sensitivity: if utilization drops to 55% the EU win shrinks to ~4% per token; if util rises to 75% it becomes ~18%. so this is sensitive to utilization assumptions.
lisa: ops question — any networking/regulatory blockers for routing customer traffic from NA to EU infra? logs/privacy?
jamie: for enterprise eu-custs we can't, but for global customers with no data residency req we can. need to flag customers with residency constraints before shifting.
billing-bot: FYI — current committed SKU inventory: NA: 250 A100, 120 H100; EU: 80 A100, 40 H100. Unallocated capacity (free headroom) in NA this quarter is ~18%.\avikas: (typo) ignore
vikas: thanks for that inventory. If we moved 30% of new commits to EU we'd need ~40 more A100-equivalents there; procurement lead time ~6-8 weeks for reserved offers.
marta: timeline seems doable before q3 starts if we decide in 2 weeks. we should run a per-customer mapping to ensure we don't break SLAs.
lisa: next steps: 1) JAMIE create a short commit-rebalance proposal with the matrix you used, include term-length sensitivity (12m vs 36m) and per-customer residency flags; 2) VIKAS validate spot-runway plan for NA; 3) MARTA run quick perf/latency risk scan for top-10 NA customers; 4) I'll sync with procurement on lead times.
jamie: on it. I'll post a follow-up doc with the numbers + a small csv mapping customers we can flex. tagging @vikas @marta @lisa — ping if you want that earlier. :thumbsup:
